about.title: About Us
mission: KNZ Legal is an innovative, solution-oriented law and consultancy firm active in international trade, finance and corporate law.
We provide our clients with strategic and reliable solutions to the complex legal processes they face in domestic and international markets.
Our team follows the dynamics of global business closely and advises clients to a high standard on international contracts, investment projects, financial regulation and arbitration proceedings.
Our aim is not only to offer legal solutions but to be a strategic partner that contributes to the growth objectives of the business world.
about.vision: To be the trusted partner of internationally active companies, investors and financial institutions, and to create long-term value for the business world by strengthening the link between law and finance.
about.heroSub: A boutique practice based in Ankara and working across borders, where law and finance sit at the same table.
about.storyTitle: Where law and finance meet, as one whole.
story: KNZ Legal was founded in Ankara in 2023 on a single observation: some know the law of a finance transaction, others know its finance; very few read both at once. Seeing the loan behind the guarantee and the project behind the loan gives a client a different kind of confidence.

Today the firm serves clients in Türkiye, the United Kingdom, the Gulf and Africa from its Ankara office. Most of our work is cross-border: foreign-owned companies, export finance, infrastructure projects and the disputes that grow out of them.
We treat being a boutique as a deliberate choice. Every file is run from start to finish by a lawyer who knows it; when a client calls, they speak to someone who knows their matter.
values: We give no legal opinion before understanding the financial logic. Cash flow, security margin and the definition of default matter to us as much as any clause.
We state the odds and the timeline at the outset: not what the client wants to hear, but what they need to know.
Your file does not pass from hand to hand; the same lawyer runs it from start to finish. Calls are returned the same day.
Five working languages, two legal systems, business relationships on three continents. When the foreign partner is at the table, you need no interpreter.

items.intro: From incorporation to shareholder relations, from M&A to liquidation, we stand with you at every stage of a company's life. As a firm that reads the Turkish Commercial Code and English company law together, we know foreign-owned structures particularly well.
items.who: Family businesses, foreign-owned ventures, holding groups and companies investing in Türkiye.
faq: How fast can a foreign company incorporate in Türkiye?

With documents in hand, incorporation via MERSİS usually completes within a week; the slow part is preparing apostilled documents and powers of attorney. We plan the process before collecting the documents.
Is a shareholders' agreement necessary?

The articles of association are public and limited; the balance between partners (exit rights, deadlock, dividends, non-compete) is set only by a shareholders' agreement. With more than one shareholder we consider it essential.

items.title: Banking and Finance Law
points: Banking and Credit Law
Loan agreements, security arrangements, mortgages and guarantees, legal review of financing structures.
Investment Law
Legal risk analysis for domestic and cross-border investment projects, investor–state disputes, investment agreements and protection mechanisms.
Financial Restructuring
Debt management, refinancing, restructuring plans and settlement processes between creditors and debtors.
Fintech and Digital Finance
Advice on electronic money, crypto assets, digital payment systems and blockchain-based financial solutions.
Capital Markets Law

International Financing
Contracts and disputes relating to letters of credit, guarantees, leasing, factoring and other international financing instruments.
items.intro: This is the heart of our daily practice: letters of guarantee, loan agreements, suretyship and pledge structures, trade finance. Because we read law and finance at the same table, we see what the bank wants, what the client is committing to and where the risk actually sits.
items.who: Construction and infrastructure companies, exporters, SMEs with standing bank relationships, fintech ventures and investors.
faq: A demand has been made under my letter of guarantee. What now?

The bank must pay on first demand; objection is possible only in narrow cases (manifest bad faith, fraud). What matters is not the moment of demand but the wording agreed when the guarantee was drafted. We assist at both stages.
What should I watch in a loan agreement?
Events of default, cross-default, margin top-up obligations and prepayment terms. Most disputes come from these four clauses.

items.title: International Trade Law
points: International Sales Contracts (CISG)
Drafting, negotiation and dispute resolution for export and import contracts.
Carriage and Delivery Contracts
Carriage, insurance and delivery contracts in line with INCOTERMS.
Payment and Security Instruments

Customs and Trade Regulation
Import and export licences, taxation, CE/FCA requirements and trade policy measures.
Foreign Investor and International Project Advisory

items.intro: Export and import contracts, INCOTERMS, documentary credits and guarantees, customs rules. Before the goods leave, we settle the contract, the payment security and which court or tribunal will decide a dispute.
items.who: Exporters, distributors, logistics companies, Turkish firms opening up to African and Gulf markets.
faq: Does the CISG apply to our contract automatically?
If the parties are in different contracting states, yes, unless excluded. Parties are often unaware of this; the contract should expressly choose or exclude it.
Letter of credit or letter of guarantee?

A letter of credit ties payment to documents and protects the buyer too; a guarantee secures against breach of an obligation. Which fits depends on the structure of the relationship; we decide together.

items.title: Real Estate Law

Land Registry and Zoning

items.intro: Property acquisitions, construction and land-for-flats contracts, leases, title and zoning matters. Our construction-group experience lets us bring a project's reality on site to the contract table.
items.who: Investors, contractors, landowners, foreigners acquiring property in Türkiye, commercial tenants and landlords.
faq: Can foreigners buy property in Türkiye?

Yes; apart from country-specific limits and military-zone checks, the process resembles a domestic purchase. A valuation report and a foreign-currency purchase certificate are mandatory; we run every step.
What protects the landowner in a land-for-flats contract?
Delivery schedule, delay penalties, timing of unit transfers and a mortgage prohibition. Execution before a notary and annotation on the title are vital.

items.title: International Arbitration
points: International Arbitration Proceedings
Representation and defence before ICC, LCIA, ICSID, ISTAC, UNCITRAL and other arbitral institutions.
Investor–State Disputes
State contracts, bilateral investment treaties (BITs) and disputes under ICSID.
Commercial Arbitration
Disputes arising from cross-border sales, joint ventures, construction, energy and finance contracts.
Recognition and Enforcement of Awards
Enforcement of foreign arbitral awards in different legal systems, including Türkiye and the United Kingdom.
Mediation and Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR)
Legal support in negotiation, mediation and settlement processes.
Arbitration Agreements and Clauses
Drafting arbitration clauses, enforceability review and dispute-prevention advice.
items.intro: Commercial and investment arbitration under ICC, LCIA, ISTAC, ICSID and UNCITRAL rules; recognition and enforcement of awards in Türkiye and the United Kingdom. Drafting the arbitration clause correctly at contract stage wins many disputes before they begin.
items.who: Parties to international contracts, foreign investors, contractors on construction and energy projects.
faq: Is arbitration always better than court?

Not always. Its advantages are a neutral forum, confidentiality, expert arbitrators and enforcement in over 170 countries under the New York Convention. Its disadvantages are cost and the absence of appeal. We decide with you according to the contract's size.
How is a foreign award enforced in Türkiye?

An enforcement action is filed before the commercial court; the court does not review the merits, only the limited refusal grounds in the New York Convention. With a well-prepared file the process is predictable.

items.title: Enforcement and Bankruptcy Law
points: Debt Collection
Collection of receivables based on bills of exchange, cheques, promissory notes, invoices and contracts before enforcement offices and courts.
Bankruptcy and Concordat
Financial restructuring of companies, concordat filings, postponement of bankruptcy and liquidation.
Pledges and Security Management
Enforcement and realisation of mortgages, pledges over movables and commercial enterprise pledges.
Enforcement Strategy
Collection strategy, debtor tracing, attachment planning and recovery optimisation.
Bankruptcy Proceedings
Liquidation of debtor companies, creditors' committee procedures, ranking of claims and asset tracing.
International Debt Recovery
Pursuit of foreign receivables and representation in the recognition and enforcement of foreign judgments.
items.intro: Debt collection, negotiable instruments, enforcement of pledges, composition (konkordato) and bankruptcy. A natural extension of our banking practice: because we know how to structure a loan, we also know how to collect a debt and how to protect a debtor.
items.who: Creditor companies and banks, companies in financial distress, guarantors and pledgors.
faq: Does konkordato really save a company?

If operations are profitable but cash is tight, yes; if the losses are structural, it only prolongs the process. We look at the numbers first, then decide between konkordato, settlement or refinancing.
A cheque bounced. How quickly can it be collected?
Enforcement for negotiable instruments is fast: objection does not stop it and attachment can follow quickly. The timeline depends on the debtor's assets; we run an asset search before starting.

items.title: Ongoing Corporate Advisory

Contract Review and Risk Analysis

HR and Employment Law Support

Financial and Commercial Compliance
AML/KYC procedures, data protection (KVKK & GDPR), competition law and internal compliance policies.
Tax and Investment Advisory
Assessment of tax risks, international investment planning and financial restructuring proposals.

Regular legal status reports, annual risk maps and strategic review meetings.
items.intro: We work as your in-house legal department: contracts, bank correspondence, board resolutions, employment questions, compliance. You call a team that knows your business, not just a lawyer.
items.who: Growing companies without a legal department, foreign groups managing Turkish subsidiaries, family businesses.
faq: What does ongoing advisory cover?

Day-to-day contract reviews, written opinions, corporate housekeeping, employee relations and a regular compliance calendar. Litigation and arbitration are a separate scope; we draw the line together at the outset.
Does it make sense for a small company?
Especially for one: a single clause in a single contract can cost more than a whole year of support.

items.title: Fortune Türkiye: "The synergy between law and AI will grow"
items.text: Fortune Türkiye's January 2026 "2026 Investment Guide" issue features an interview with Kaan Zabtiyeoğulları. He argues that the most visible transformation in financial services is regulatory: payment infrastructures, data flows and compliance mechanisms are being reshaped, and while AI-assisted systems speed up processes, data security, algorithmic transparency and regulatory compliance become far more critical.
items.note: The interview continues in Fortune Türkiye's January 2026 issue. Original language: Turkish.
qa: Could you briefly tell us about yourself and your professional journey so far?

I work in finance law. In Türkiye my practice is in financial transactions and regulation; in the United Kingdom my work focuses more on the technical and analytical side of finance. My LLM and my professional research helped me develop an interdisciplinary perspective. While practising, I also follow academic developments closely.
Which dynamics have changed most in your sector in recent years, and how have you adapted?

The most visible transformation has been in regulation. Payment infrastructures, data flows and compliance mechanisms in particular are being reshaped. I follow this through my academic work and through international fairs and panels in finance and law, and try to adapt to the changing models.
How is digitalisation affecting your sector?

The relationship between lawyers and digitalisation is a balance of blessing and burden. AI-assisted systems speed up processes, while data security, algorithmic transparency and regulatory compliance become far more critical. These developments have to be assessed together with the technological infrastructure and the expectations of international regulators.
In a constantly changing world, what is your strategy for staying current and making a difference?

To stay current I keep in touch with academia and follow the literature and the professional communities at the intersection of law and finance. Through the seminars of think tanks in Europe and Asia, I track global trends.

kaan.name: Kaan Zabtiyeoğulları
kaan.tagline: From letters of guarantee to project finance: a lawyer who reads the law and the finance of a banking transaction together.
bio: Kaan Zabtiyeoğulları is the founder of KNZ Legal. A lawyer admitted to the Ankara Bar and a finance professional, he works across international trade, corporate, banking and finance law, and infrastructure and project finance. A large part of his day-to-day practice is banking work: letters of guarantee, loan agreements, suretyship and pledge structures, and trade finance.

He read law at Bilkent University and holds an LLM in Finance Law from the University of Sussex. He completed the Executive Finance Programme at the University of Oxford's Saïd Business School and is pursuing the MIT MicroMasters in Finance. During Uppsala University's international arbitration programme he worked with the Swedish firm Vinge on a pharmaceutical distribution dispute.

He combines legal practice with hands-on finance experience: compliance (AML/KYC) and trade finance at a trade finance bank; arbitration and project work at an energy and infrastructure law firm; financial modelling, bank financings and overseas project appraisal as financial and legal analyst at a construction group; finance director of a UK social enterprise; and research assistant in development economics and public finance at a university.

He served as a delegate to the United Nations Committee on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities in Geneva with an ELSA delegation, and held professional development (STEP) leadership roles at ELSA Ankara and ELSA Türkiye. Through work as a translator for the Embassy of Senegal and water-facility projects in Ethiopia with the Ankara Rotary Club, he maintains working connections in West and East Africa.

His comparative article on the pricing of green bonds is appearing in the Journal of Energy Law Research; his empirical paper on commodity price spillovers and banking sector risk in emerging markets is under review. His writing on sukuk and infrastructure finance, sovereign debt and sanctions, and fintech regulation is published on this site.
